title: Lipid Fraction Extraction and Analysis of Ewe's Milk Samples
author: Évelyn ilva de Melo Soares
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b3xsqpne

steps.title: Perform Lipid Extraction Method 1 (Direct)
steps.instruction: Extract and derivatize lipids directly from ewe's milk using n-hexane.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of ewe's milk to 2 mL of 0.5 M NaOH solution in methanol in a 15 mL centrifuge tube with screw cap and Teflon septum.
Heat in a water bath at 60°C for 5 min, then cool to room temperature.
Add 3 mL of esterifying solution (composed of 15 mL H2SO4, 10 g NH4Cl, and 300 mL methanol).
Heat in a water bath at 60°C for 2 min, then cool to room temperature.
Add 2 mL of saturated NaCl aqueous solution and agitate thoroughly.
Add 4 mL of hexane and vortex for 30 s.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 2000 rpm.
Remove the supernatant containing the fatty acid methyl esters (FAMEs) for GC-FID analysis.

steps.title: Perform Lipid Extraction Method 2 (Chloroform-Methanol)
steps.instruction: Extract lipids using a cold chloroform-methanol-water mixture.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of milk sample to a 50 mL centrifuge tube with screw cap and Teflon septum.
Add 5, 10, or 15 mL of a cold extracting mixture of chloroform–methanol–water (ratio 2:1:1 v/v/v).
Vortex for 2 min and then place on ultrasound for 20 min.
Add 1 mL of chloroform and 0.5 mL of 2.0 M KCl solution, then stir in the vortex for 1 min.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 2500 rpm.
Collect the lower layer (lipid extract), evaporate under nitrogen flow, and reserve for derivatization.

steps.title: Derivatize Extracted Lipids
steps.instruction: Perform transesterification via methylation on the lipid phase extracted in Method 2.

substeps.instruction: Add 2.0 mL of 0.5 methanolic sodium hydroxide solution to the glass tube containing the extracted lipid.
Heat in a water bath at 60°C for 5 min, then cool to room temperature.
Immediately add 5.0 mL of esterifying reagent solution (15 mL H2SO4, 10 g NH4Cl, and 300 mL methanol).
Heat in a water bath at 60°C for 2 min, then cool to room temperature.
Add 2 mL of saturated NaCl solution and agitate thoroughly.
Add 4 mL of hexane to extract the FAMEs.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 2000 rpm.
Remove an aliquot of the supernatant and place in a 2-mL bottle with a lid for GC-FID analysis.

steps.title: Analyze FAMEs by GC-FID
steps.instruction: Determine the fatty acid profile using a gas chromatograph with a flame ionization detector.

substeps.instruction: Use a Shimadzu GC 2010 equipped with a fused silica capillary column (CP–BPX-70, 30 m × 0.25 mm, 0.25 μm) and a flame ionization detector.
Set carrier gas to helium (99.999% purity).
Inject 1 µL of sample using an AOC 20i automatic injector (10-µL syringe) in 50:1 split mode.
Set injector and detector temperatures to 250°C.
Program the column heating ramp: 80°C for 3 min, then increase at 10°C/min to 140°C, then increase at 5°C/min to 250°C, and hold at 250°C for 5 min (total analysis time: 40 min).
Determine peak areas and retention times using Shimadzu Lab solutions software and identify FAs by comparing retention times with FAMEs standards.
